messages.subject: Trouble with storing peakPick object
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am completely new to R, so this might be a stupid question. I am playing around with cardinal using a dataset containing 44032 features and 4981 pixels. When I run the peakPick function on the data set at pixel=1 everything works fine and a plot is generated. When I try the same function on the whole dataset and storing the results into a new object I get the following error:

> data2 <- peakPick(data, method="simple", SNR=3)
peakPeak: Using method = simple
  |============================================================================================| 100%
Error in validObject(object) :
  invalid class “MSImageData” object: 1: number of non-NA indices in positionArray must match number of cols of data elements
invalid class “MSImageData” object: 2: number of non-NA indices in positionArray must match number of rows of coord

There appears to be a mismatch between the matrices of data and data2? Do I have to make changes to my data matrix prior to running pickPeak?

Any help is greatly appreciated!

messages.subject: Re: How can I plot ROC for SSCG data?
messages.subject_clean: How can I plot ROC for SSCG data?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shadrack,

What you're trying to do doesn't make sense for the method. The spatial shrunken centroids method uses ALL of the masses to predict the segments, so there is no way to get the accuracy for only a specific mass.

Printing the summary of cross-validated results will print the specificity and sensitivity for the fitted model. And ranking the m/z values by t-statistic using the topLabels method will show the order of importance of each mass for distinguishing each segment.

The latter may be closest to what you want, if you're trying to find the importance of each mass in distinguishing a particular segment from the others.

-Kylie

messages.body_plain:
Hi Vadim,

Can you try running :

any(duplicated(coord(data)))

If it returns TRUE, then you somehow have duplicated pixel coordinates.

If that is the case, a quick fix (which throws away pixel with duplicated coordinates) would be:

data <- data[,!duplicated(coord(data))]

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Trouble with storing peakPick object
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vadim,

Good to hear it works. The main reason I've encountered this is when coordinates are stored as decimals rather than integers. Cardinal implicitly rounds them to integers, since it expects a regular pixel grid, so some pixels may be rounded to share coordinates that were different by a decimal.  If there is a reason you need more control over the pixel coordinates, you may want to write your own function to transform the coordinates to integers more correctly.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Plotting intensity value at pixel center in image
messages.subject_clean: Plotting intensity value at pixel center in image
messages.body_plain:
Hi Heath,

No, there is not simple built-in way of doing that.

The easiest interactive way I can think of would be to plot the image using select(mode="pixel"), then get the coordinates from that, and use text() to plot the intensities. If you already know the coordinates, then just use text().

-Kylie

messages.subject: Reading imzML files in
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shadrack,

This is caused by having spectra with measurements at 0 m/z, which causes errors during certain calculations required during import when using "units.accuracy='ppm'" (the default). Try using "units.accuracy='mz'" instead. This will set a fixed bin size rather than an adaptive one. Make sure to change "mass.accuracy=" to your desired bin size, since the default doesn't make sense for m/z units.

-Kylie
